caveats: CPU/RAM/local SSD included. Billing one-minute increments from launch health-check success to termination, including idle. Per-GPU price changes with node count. No spot list found.
Any null count, CPU/RAM, billing increment or minimum is unverified, not unlimited/free.
This is GPU-product research, not a claim that every feature of the entire vendor documentation was audited. Unverified features are null.
GPU multi-count bundles, variant/region selection and fractional slices require a SKU-aware estimator; unsupported rows remain unpriced in strict cards.

Modes with gpu=null are intentionally excluded, not free GPU modes. Never substitute 0 for a null rate. Flags alt indicate DIY/ML infrastructure, not the same thing as managed untrusted-code sandboxes.
Unknown fee, storage or bandwidth means full monthly total may be unavailable. Rates exclude taxes.

Instances include local SSD (512 GiB to 4 TiB by SKU; card uses the 512 GiB minimum). Persistent filesystems are billed per GiB-month in hourly increments; docs quote $0.20/GiB-month only as an example ("might not reflect current pricing"), so no filesystem rate is encoded. Filesystems have no ingress/egress charges.
GH200 (on-demand-gh200-1) is an Arm (Grace) host: x86 containers may not run.
No stop/suspend: instances can only be launched, restarted or terminated; 'sudo shutdown' puts the instance in Alert status and billing continues. Idle GPU time is billed at the full rate.
Weekly invoicing; refunds only as service credits that expire after 12 months; major credit cards only.
Filesystem usage cannot be capped; up to 24 filesystems per account; us-south-1 filesystems limited to 10 TB; filesystems must be attached at launch and are region-bound.

fleet.notes: New-account instance cap (number unpublished) grows automatically as invoices are paid. Cloud API launch endpoint is rate-limited to 1 request / 12 s (5 per minute), one instance per launch request; general API 1 req/s. Credit card required (no debit/prepaid), $10 refundable pre-auth; purchases only from listed countries.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated. To preserve state, we recommend using Docker to containerize your environment and performing regular backups of important data.
snapshot_auto.note: No stop/sleep state at all; terminate discards the instance and its local SSD. Only attached filesystems persist.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Cloud API has no snapshot or custom-image endpoints (images endpoint only lists Lambda-provided base images).

harness_api.note: Cloud API covers instances, filesystems, firewall rules, images, SSH keys, audit events, tickets only; no agent harness or exec API.

egress_allowlist.quote: You can restrict incoming traffic to the instances in a workspace, including 1-Click Cluster management (head) nodes, by creating firewall rules on the Firewall page in the Lambda Cloud console.
egress_allowlist.note: Firewall rules and rulesets are inbound-only (API: 'List inbound firewall rules'; FirewallRule has source_network only). No outbound/egress controls documented; restrict egress in-guest if needed.

egress_http_rules.quote: You can restrict incoming traffic to the instances in a workspace
egress_http_rules.note: No provider-side egress control of any kind, so no HTTP-level rules.

ingress_rules.quote: By default, Lambda allows only incoming ICMP traffic or TCP traffic on port 22 (SSH).
ingress_rules.note: Global workspace rules (up to 100) plus per-instance rulesets (up to 128, attach at launch only); TCP/UDP port ranges and source IPv4/CIDR; managed via console or Cloud API.

guest_firewall.note: On-demand instances are VMs with root/sudo (virtio disks /dev/vda in docs' df output); iptables/nftables inside the guest should work. Not stated explicitly.

volume_attach.quote: A filesystem is a unit of networked persistent storage you can connect to your instance.
volume_attach.note: NFS-backed filesystems mounted at /lambda/nfs/<name> (custom mount points via file_system_mounts); must be attached at launch ('Filesystems can't be attached to running instances'), same region; up to 24 per account; 8 EB (10 TB in us-south-1). No block volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Lambda filesystems are automatically created and attached to each 1CC node, and can also be attached to Lambda On-Demand instances.
volume_shared.note: Read-write NFS filesystem mounted by several instances/nodes at once. OpenAPI Filesystem schema (https://cloud.lambda.ai/api/v1/openapi.json): 'Information about a shared filesystem.'; filesystems doc: 'Your filesystem must be detached from all instances before it can be deleted.' Also remote access via Filesystem S3 Adapter in select regions; not mountable remotely via NFS.

isolation.quote: By default, each ODC instance runs Ubuntu 22.04 LTS.
isolation.note: Lambda Cloud on-demand instances are dedicated VM-like GPU rental instances (root/sudo, virtio block devices per docs' df output). Lambda does not publicly name the hypervisor; existing card already records isolation as "vm" (full VM), so qemu-kvm is the closest enumerated match. Not explicitly confirmed as KVM/QEMU by name.

image_oci.quote: By default, each ODC instance runs Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack... You can also choose an alternative base image instead. Available image types include: Lambda Stack... GPU Base...
image_oci.note: Only a fixed menu of Lambda-provided base images (Lambda Stack, GPU Base, etc.) is offered; the Cloud API images endpoint only lists Lambda-provided images. No bring-your-own Docker/OCI machine image support.

fork.note: No snapshot/custom-image/clone capability exists to fork a machine into new ones.

fork_running.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
fork_running.note: No fork capability at all, so no running-clone capability.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: No snapshot or fork mechanism of any kind, so no memory-inclusive fork.

wake_on_request.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated. ... 'sudo shutdown' puts the instance in Alert status and billing continues.
wake_on_request.note: There is no stop/sleep state to wake from; idle instances keep running and billing until explicitly terminated.

auto_stop_idle.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
auto_stop_idle.note: Idle GPU time is billed at the full rate; instances do not auto-stop/sleep on idle.

live_resize.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
live_resize.note: No API/console action to change CPU/RAM/GPU of a running instance; you must terminate and relaunch a different instance type.

agent_harnesses.quote: Lambda Stack: The default image used on most ODC instances. Includes: NVIDIA driver, CUDA toolkit, OFED, cuDNN, NCCL, Lambda Stack Python packages (PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX), Docker, JupyterLab.
agent_harnesses.note: Base images bundle ML frameworks and JupyterLab, not coding-agent harnesses (Claude Code/Codex/OpenCode) as templates.

own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Cloud API only covers instances, filesystems, firewall rules, images, SSH keys, audit events, tickets — no first-party browser/computer-use/research agent.

mcp_server.note: No Lambda-published MCP server for controlling Lambda Cloud instances was found in Lambda's docs or GitHub org.

lang_node.quote: By default, each ODC instance runs Ubuntu 22.04 LTS. Lambda also preinstalls Lambda Stack...
lang_node.note: Instances are full root/sudo Ubuntu VMs; Node.js can be installed/apt-installed like on any Ubuntu box, though it is not preinstalled by default (Lambda Stack focuses on Python/CUDA).

inbound_https.quote: By default, Lambda allows only incoming ICMP traffic or TCP traffic on port 22 (SSH).
inbound_https.note: Instances have a public IPv4 and configurable inbound TCP firewall rules, so HTTPS (443/other ports) can be opened and reached directly; there is no managed HTTPS URL/proxy layer, just raw TCP ingress control.

secret_proxy.quote: On-demand GPU cloud instances billed by the minute for training and inference workloads.
secret_proxy.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; no first-party credential-injecting HTTP proxy documented. Secrets would be handled as env vars/files/SSH-mounted config only.

static_egress_ip.quote: Connection options # You connect to your instance through a standard SSH connection.
static_egress_ip.note: No reserved/elastic IP product is documented; each instance gets a public IPv4 but there is no stated guarantee of a fixed, reusable outbound IP across relaunches.

windows.quote: os: ["linux"] for all on-demand instance modes.
windows.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; all on-demand GPU instance types are Linux (Ubuntu 22.04 LTS) only.

macos.quote: os: ["linux"] for all on-demand instance modes.
macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Lambda is an NVIDIA GPU cloud, no Apple hardware/macOS instances.

self_host.quote: On-demand GPU cloud instances billed by the minute for training and inference workloads.
self_host.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Lambda Cloud is a managed hosted service run on Lambda's own datacenters, not self-hostable software.

byoc.quote: On-demand GPU cloud instances billed by the minute for training and inference workloads.
byoc.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Lambda sells capacity in its own/partner datacenters (Public Cloud, Private Cloud), not a managed deployment into the customer's own cloud account.

open_source.quote: On-demand GPU cloud instances billed by the minute for training and inference workloads.
open_source.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Lambda Cloud is a proprietary managed service (Lambda Stack itself is a curated software bundle, not the cloud control plane).

eu_data_residency.note: Lambda offers an EU region (europe-central-1, Germany) for on-demand instances, allowing customers to keep machines/data in the EU.

max_session_h.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
max_session_h.note: On-demand instances run indefinitely (billed continuously, including idle) until the customer explicitly terminates them; no maximum session duration is imposed by Lambda.

snapshot.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated. To preserve state, we recommend using Docker to containerize your environment and performing regular backups of important data.
snapshot.note: Docs' own 'Suspending an instance' section confirms there is no snapshot/suspend capability at all; Cloud API (openapi.json) exposes only /instance-operations/launch, /restart, /terminate — no snapshot or image-create endpoints.

pause_resume.quote: At the moment, Lambda Cloud instances can only be launched, restarted, or terminated.
pause_resume.note: Same section explicitly states there is no pause/suspend mechanism; a manual in-guest 'sudo shutdown' just puts the instance in Alert status while billing continues (per the caveat text right above this quote in the docs), it does not stop billing or free the GPU. Cloud API instance-operations are limited to launch/restart/terminate.

custom_image.quote: "summary": "List available images", "description": "Retrieves a list of available images by region."
custom_image.note: The only images-related Cloud API endpoint (GET /api/v1/images) lists Lambda-provided base images by region; there is no POST/create-image or upload-image endpoint, and the instance-launch payload only accepts an image id from that list, not a user-supplied custom image/AMI.

hipaa.quote: Security and compliance + SOC 2 Type II attestation. ISO 27001, 27017, 27701, and 22301 certified. Strict access controls, MFA, continuous monitoring. Customer-governed access (revoke Lambda credentials anytime).
hipaa.note: Lambda's Trust page and Trust Portal (SafeBase, trust.lambda.ai) enumerate SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001/27017/27701/22301, and CCPA compliance in detail but do not list HIPAA or a BAA program anywhere on the trust/security pages, pricing page, or docs. No HIPAA-eligible service or BAA offering was found after checking the trust page, trust portal, and llms.txt; treated as not offered.
